facts.text: Woodside originated as a rural crossroads in the mid‑18th century, with buildings dating to 1765, now an affluent suburb preserving vernacular architecture.
The Lenape first inhabited the area, using fertile lands near the Delaware River before European arrival.
Quaker settlers fleeing persecution, families like the Yardleys, Houghes, and Palmers received 500‑acre grants that shaped early road patterns.
Woodside once sat at the crossroads of Stony Hill Road and Yardley‑Langhorne Road, a stagecoach link between Philadelphia and New York.
In 1979, preservation efforts earned Woodside a local historic district designation and a National Register of Historic Places listing.
A fieldstone inn built by Jesse Palmer in 1765 once served travelers, now a historic landmark in Woodside.
